section: NITI Aayog - structure, mandate, verticals, differences from the Planning Commission
subsections: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the approach adopted by NITI Aayog for fostering cooperative federalism?
o: Allocating centrally sponsored grants to States
Imposing uniform plans on all States
Restricting State participation to annual plan discussions
Bringing States together on a single platform through a bottom-up approach
accepted.x: NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism by bringing States together on a common platform through a bottom-up approach.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional approach rather than confusing it with the former top-down planning model.
accepted.sec: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

accepted.s: State rankings in the SDG Index, Health Index and Fiscal Health Index primarily reflect which function of NITI Aayog?
accepted.x: State rankings in areas such as SDG, health and fiscal health foster competitive federalism while also encouraging intergovernmental cooperation.
accepted.tq: Link an institutional activity with the federal principle it promotes.
accepted.sec: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four mandate areas listed for NITI Aayog in the India Year Book 2026?
accepted.x: The four mandate areas are knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation. Direct allocation of plan grants is not a mandate area of NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Find the option that belongs to the former Planning Commission rather than NITI Aayog.
accepted.sec: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NITI Aayog:
1. It aims to build credible village-level plans and aggregate them upwards.
2. It functions as the government's think tank.
3. It is described as a directional and policy dynamo.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the planning and policy role of NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Use the broad institutional description to identify the combination containing all correct statements.
accepted.sec: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

accepted.s: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) is best described as:
o: A constitutional body supervising State finances
A fund-allocation division of the Union Finance Ministry
An autonomous institute conducting population census operations
An attached office of NITI Aayog monitoring and evaluating schemes
accepted.x: DMEO is an attached office of NITI Aayog concerned with monitoring and evaluation of schemes and policies.
accepted.tq: Match the body with its institutional status and principal function.

accepted.s: DMEO was established in 2015 by merging which two organisations?
accepted.x: DMEO was set up in 2015 through the merger of the Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) and the Independent Evaluation Office (IEO).
accepted.tq: Test the merger pair directly, a common organisational-identity trap.

accepted.s: The major shift associated with the work of DMEO is from monitoring expenditure to:
accepted.x: DMEO represents a shift from expenditure monitoring towards outcome and impact evaluation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the older input or expenditure focus from the outcome-based evaluation approach.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) 2.0:
1. It was launched in 2024.
2. It has an outlay of Rs 2,750 crore.
3. It is scheduled to continue up to March 2028.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: AIM 2.0 was launched in 2024 with an allocation of Rs 2,750 crore and is intended to run until March 2028.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical and time-bound detail before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: AIM 2.0 primarily seeks to:
o: Fill ecosystem gaps and scale innovations
accepted.x: AIM 2.0 is intended to fill gaps in the innovation ecosystem and scale up innovations.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated objective rather than the institutional location of the programme.

accepted.s: NILERD, associated with NITI Aayog, is:
o: An attached office formed by merging PEO and IEO
A regional council chaired by the Prime Minister
An autonomous institute formerly known as IAMR
accepted.x: NILERD is an autonomous institute under NITI Aayog and was formerly known as the Institute of Applied Manpower Research (IAMR).
accepted.tq: Separate an autonomous institute from an attached office and a council.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SETU:
1. SETU stands for State Economic and Transformation Units.
2. SETUs are created under the State Support Mission.
3. The Steering Committee of SETU is chaired by the CEO of NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: SETU means State Economic and Transformation Units; they are created under the State Support Mission, whose SETU Steering Committee is chaired by the CEO of NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym first and then verify its administrative placement and chairperson.

accepted.s: Which NITI Aayog vertical leads the engagement of States with the Centre?
accepted.x: The Team India Hub is responsible for leading engagement between the States and the Centre.
accepted.tq: Match the functional description with the correct named vertical.

accepted.s: The Knowledge and Innovation Hub of NITI Aayog is primarily concerned with:
accepted.x: The Knowledge and Innovation Hub builds think-tank capacity within the NITI Aayog framework.
accepted.tq: Distinguish knowledge-capacity building from monitoring and federal coordination functions.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the State Support Mission?
o: It is an umbrella initiative under which States establish SETUs to draft State Vision@2047.
It is a programme limited to promoting school innovation.
It is an attached office that evaluates Union ministries.
It is the successor to the National Development Council for approving national plans.
accepted.x: The State Support Mission is an umbrella initiative through which States establish SETUs to prepare State Vision@2047 documents.
accepted.tq: Select the option combining the body’s status, mechanism and stated planning purpose.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Assam’s State-level institution is SITA, while Maharashtra’s corresponding institution is MITRA.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure State-institution pair and eliminate the swapped names.

accepted.s: Which of the following programmes is run by NITI Aayog in addition to the SDG India Index?
accepted.x: NITI Aayog runs both the Aspirational Districts Programme and the SDG India Index.
accepted.tq: Recognise the directly associated flagship programme and reject bodies from the earlier planning structure.

accepted.s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog was first constituted in February 2015 and reconstituted in:
accepted.x: The Governing Council was first constituted in February 2015 and reconstituted in February 2021.
accepted.tq: Use the paired dates and select the precise reconstitution year.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog:
1. It includes the Prime Minister.
2. It includes the Chief Ministers of all States.
3. It includes the Chief Ministers of Union Territories having legislatures.
4. It includes the Lieutenant Governors of other Union Territories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Governing Council comprises the Prime Minister, all State Chief Ministers, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with legislatures, and Lieutenant Governors of the remaining Union Territories, along with specified NITI Aayog members and invitees.
accepted.tq: Check the complete composition rather than treating Union Territories as a single category.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a member category of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
accepted.x: The Governing Council includes the Vice-Chairperson, full-time members and special invitees, but judges of all High Courts are not a prescribed member category.
accepted.tq: Find the institutionally unrelated category in the composition list.

accepted.s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog has taken over the work of which body?
accepted.x: The Governing Council has taken over the work earlier associated with the National Development Council.
accepted.tq: Identify the predecessor body whose planning-related role was transferred.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the meetings of the Governing Council:
1. It usually meets once a year.
2. Its frequency is prescribed by a fixed statutory schedule.
3. The 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Governing Council generally meets once a year, and its 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026. Its frequency is not fixed by statute.
accepted.tq: Spot the false absolute claim about statutory frequency while retaining the date-based statement.

accepted.s: The theme of the 11th meeting of the Governing Council held on 11 June 2026 was:
o: Innovation and Growth for Atmanirbhar Bharat
Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047
accepted.x: The 11th Governing Council meeting was held under the theme “Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the themes of the 10th and 11th meetings.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the 10th meeting of the Governing Council?
o: It was held in 2024 with the theme “State Vision@2047”.
It was held in 2025 with the theme “Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
It was held in 2026 with the theme “Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
It was held in 2025 with the theme “Knowledge and Innovation for Bharat@2047”.
accepted.x: The 10th meeting was held in 2025 and had the theme “Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
accepted.tq: Separate two closely related meeting themes by matching each with its year and meeting number.

accepted.s: At the 11th meeting of the Governing Council, which attendance-related fact was recorded for the first time?
o: All 28 Chief Ministers attended the meeting
All Lieutenant Governors attended the meeting
All Union Ministers attended the meeting
accepted.x: The meeting recorded 100% attendance of Chief Ministers, with all 28 Chief Ministers attending for the first time.
accepted.tq: Use the precise number and the qualifying phrase “for the first time”.

accepted.s: Regional Councils of NITI Aayog are constituted primarily to deal with:
o: Allocation of funds to individual districts
Issues affecting more than one State
accepted.x: Regional Councils address issues that affect more than one State.
accepted.tq: Match the council type with the geographical scope of the issues it handles.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the leadership of a Regional Council of NITI Aayog?
o: It is convened by the President and chaired by the Vice-President.
It is convened by the Governor and jointly headed by two Chief Ministers.
It is permanently chaired by the Finance Minister alone.
It is convened by the Prime Minister and jointly headed by a rotating group Chief Minister and a Union Minister.
accepted.x: The Prime Minister convenes Regional Councils, which are jointly headed by a rotating group Chief Minister and a Central Minister.
accepted.tq: Ask who convenes the body and who jointly heads it to avoid authority swaps.

accepted.s: Which of the following may form part of a Regional Council besides the rotating group Chief Minister and Central Minister?
o: Central and State Ministers, secretaries, domain experts and a support cell in NITI Aayog
accepted.x: Regional Councils may include Central and State ministers, secretaries, domain experts and a support cell in NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Select the option that gives the complete supporting composition rather than an exclusive category.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Planning Commission from NITI Aayog with respect to financial powers?
o: NITI Aayog allocates funds, whereas the Planning Commission was only advisory.
The Planning Commission allocated plan funds and grants, whereas NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power and is advisory.
Both bodies possessed identical powers to allocate plan funds.
Neither body had any role in economic planning.
accepted.x: The Planning Commission allocated plan funds and grants. NITI Aayog does not have fund-allocation power and functions as an advisory institution.
accepted.tq: Compare the operative financial power rather than the common planning-related purpose.

accepted.s: Which approach is correctly associated with NITI Aayog rather than the Planning Commission?
o: Bottom-up planning based on cooperative federalism
Planning exclusively through the National Development Council
accepted.x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach and promotes cooperative federalism, unlike the Planning Commission’s top-down, one-size-fits-all planning.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed comparison trap between top-down and bottom-up approaches.

accepted.s: With reference to the role of States, which statement is correct?
o: NITI Aayog restricts States to annual plan talks.
Under the Planning Commission every Chief Minister was a permanent member of its Governing Council.
Under NITI Aayog every Chief Minister sits on the Governing Council, giving States a direct role.
The Planning Commission gave States a direct role through its Governing Council.
accepted.x: The Planning Commission limited the role of States largely to the National Development Council and annual plan discussions, whereas NITI Aayog gives every Chief Minister a direct role through its Governing Council.
accepted.tq: Track the institutional location of State participation and reject the swapped-body statements.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares the top officials of the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog?
o: Planning Commission—Vice-Chairperson and CEO; NITI Aayog—Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary
Planning Commission—Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary; NITI Aayog—Vice-Chairperson and CEO
accepted.x: The Planning Commission had a Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary, while NITI Aayog has a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO appointed by the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Use the paired office titles to detect an authority and designation swap.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding membership of the two institutions:
1. The Planning Commission could have up to eight full-time members.
2. The Planning Commission had no part-time members.
3. NITI Aayog may have full-time members and up to two part-time members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Planning Commission had up to eight full-time members and no part-time members. NITI Aayog includes full-time members and may have up to two part-time members.
accepted.tq: Compare numerical composition details across both institutions before selecting the combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the planning documents associated with NITI Aayog?
o: It has retained the exact planning format of the Planning Commission.
It prepares plans exclusively for Union ministries.
It prepares only one-size-fits-all Five-Year Plans.
It follows a Vision-Strategy-Action Agenda through a bottom-up approach.
accepted.x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up planning model expressed through the Vision-Strategy-Action Agenda, unlike the Planning Commission’s one-size-fits-all Five-Year Plans.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the newer planning framework from the former Five-Year Plan format.

accepted.s: Planning Commission plans were placed for approval before which body?
o: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog
accepted.x: Plans prepared by the Planning Commission were placed before the National Development Council for approval.
accepted.tq: Identify the approval body associated with the former planning process.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the present status of the National Development Council is correct?
o: It has become a Regional Council of NITI Aayog.
It is now inactive because its role has passed to NITI Aayog’s Governing Council.
It allocates funds to ministries under NITI Aayog.
It actively approves the current Five-Year Plans of NITI Aayog.
accepted.x: The National Development Council is now inactive, as its role was transferred to the Governing Council of NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional succession principle to distinguish the inactive body from its successor.
